item.title: Ben James Seizes Weekend Lead At World Wide Technology Championship
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Ben James took control of the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship on Friday night in Los Cabos. The rookie’s aggressive 64 (8-under) moved him to 129 (15-under) after 36 holes at El Cardonal at Diamante, a course designed by Tiger Woods. Darkness forced a suspension of play at 5:48 p.m. local time, leaving 12 golfers on the course to finish their rounds on Saturday morning. James now holds a one-shot lead heading into the weekend, according to Sportsnet.ca reporting from the field. During the second round, James made five straight birdies around the turn. He capped the round with a final birdie on the ninth hole. Since turning professional out of Virginia this summer, this performance represents his 14th round of 65 or lower across just 13 tournaments. This victory would secure a spot on the 2028 Championship Series under the new model and move the team into the top 50 in world rankings. Adapting to Professional Pressure James acknowledged the shift in scoring ability required at this level compared to his collegiate days. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” Malnati Chases Contention Peter Malnati sat tied for the lead until a critical error on the par-3 ninth hole. He fell short of the green and missed a 12-foot par putt, concluding his round of 64. The missed opportunity left him one shot behind James. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where … I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair shot a 68 to sit three shots behind the leader. Sudarshan Yellamaraju of Mississauga, Ont.James was six shots ahead, He is the top Canadian at 10 under. Ben Silverman of Thornhill, Ont., finished at 9 under, while Adam Svensson of Surrey, B.C., was at 7 under. Nick Taylor of Abbotsford, B.C., also made the cut at 5 under. Defending champion Ben Griffin and fellow North Carolina Tar Heel Ryan Gerard headline the field, with Griffin being one of six past champions competing in Cabo, per Central Oregon Daily . Cut Line and Schedule Saturday morning will see the 36-hole cut announced. Late Friday, 75 golfers were projected to make the cut at 5 under, although two players on the number still needed to finish their second rounds. item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-ARSENAL-HULL - AFP Arsenal cemented their place at the top of the Premier League table with a gritty 1-0 victory over Hull City at the Emirates Stadium. A 72nd-minute strike from captain Martin Odegaard finally pierced a resilient five-man Hull defence. It was a tactical battle of attrition at the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal eventually wore down a remarkably disciplined Hull City side. The Gunners dominated 67 per cent of the ball and fired off 21 shots, yet they found clear-cut opportunities difficult to come by against the Tigers' low block. A controversial first-half VAR decision to deny Kai Havertz a penalty for offside added to the tension, leaving Mikel Arteta and the home crowd increasingly frustrated as the game remained goalless at the break. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 72nd minute through the persistent Martin Odegaard, who found the space to beat the impressive Konstantinos Tzolakis. While Arsenal's xG of 1.39 suggests they weren't at their creative best, their defensive solidity ensured that Hull’s rare counter-attacks were neutralised effectively. This narrow 1-0 win underscores the Gunners' ability to find solutions against deep-lying defensive structures, even when their primary attacking rhythms are disrupted. item.title: Jared McCain rediscovers outside jumper in OKC's win over Grizzlies
item.description: On a pair of catch-and-shoot looks, Jared McCain rediscovered his groove. His undermanned squad quickly put up a double-digit lead. They can thank their en-fuego-style outside shooting for that. After a cold spell, the 22-year-old showed what the positive side of his shooting variance can look like. The Oklahoma City Thunder looked their best since Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) started with a 124-97 win over the Memphis Grizzlies . The butt-whooping was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B stage. McCain finished with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting and five rebounds. He shot 3-of-8 from 3. He also had four steals and one block. Do you think McCain heard Bennett Stirtz's footsteps coming for his playing time? He's certainly played like somebody with a fire lit underneath his seat. Showing an inkling of confidence, the microwave scorer was hot throughout the night. Sure, the outside jumpers fell. But his scoring attack within the paint has also been a nice surprise so far. "Getting those transition shots where you got to guard Ajay, me or Shai, them driving to the basket is awesome for us," McCain said. "They make great decisions. For us, we just continue that. At halftime, we just kept our foot on the pedal." McCain had 12 points in the first quarter. He helped the Thunder get away from this one early. As Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gladly took a backseat after back-to-back 40-point nights, it was he and Ajay Mitchell who delivered OKC's first lethal punch to Memphis. The two absolutely demoralized the hot-shot, young, up-and-coming squad. This is what the best version of McCain looks like. When he's zoned in, he needs little time to drop points in a flurry. The Thunder have learned to play a team-friendly offensive style that lessens the burden on Gilgeous-Alexander. This is what it tangibly looks like. He made OKC's decision to start him look like an absolute genius move. "I think we're just playing together on a string. Defensively, we know what each other brings before and in the season, obviously," McCain said. "And then when people got hurt, we had to kinda figure it out. Now, we kinda know each other. We know certain things we like to do on the defensive end." This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Jared McCain rediscovers outside jumper in OKC's win over Grizzlies

item.title: Non-league match postponed after player suffers medical emergency in warm-up
item.description: A National League South match between Truro City and Folkestone Invicta was postponed on Saturday after a player suffered a medical emergency during the warm-up. Yassine En-Neyah, 26, required medical assistance while warming up for Truro and was subsequently rushed to hospital. Kick-off was initially pushed back before the match was ultimately postponed at 3:14pm GMT, 14 minutes after the original start time. “Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed,” Truro’s statement read. Club Statement: Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed. The midfielder returned to Ireland for spells at top-flight clubs Shelbourne and Waterford after not having his contract renewed at Forest in 2021, before moving to Truro for his first spell at the Cornwall club in February 2023. item.title: Concerning Deshaun Watson Update Surfaces Amid Shedeur Sanders News
item.description: A concerning update about Deshaun Watson emerged on Friday. It came amid the Cleveland Browns’ announcement that Shedeur Sanders will start for them in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints. Watson suffered a concussion last Sunday during Cleveland’s 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The league takes these cases seriously and players need to pass a series of tests before they are cleared to return to action. The star quarterback has appeared and started in the first eight games of the season. He has 163-of-249 completions for 1,806 yards and seven touchdowns against three interceptions. Watson joined the Browns in March 2022 following a trade from the Houston Texans. He then signed a fully guaranteed, five-year, $230 million deal, making it the largest guaranteed contract in NFL history at the time. The former Clemson star entered the league in 2017 as the No. 17 overall pick. Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) after the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Huntington Bank Field. Worrying Deshaun Watson News Emerges on Friday Deshaun Watson returned to practice on Friday but remains in concussion protocol. He missed the sessions in the previous two games, with Sanders taking first team reps. The second-year quarterback has been named the QB1 for Sunday. ESPN’s Adam Schefter issued an update on Watson’s condition. “Deshaun Watson was checked for a concussion during the game, cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol during the game, and then shortly after the game reported symptoms to the team,” Schefter said. “And at that point, they knew he would end up in the concussion protocol. So (he) did not practice Wednesday and Thursday (but) was able to practice today. “(He) has not cleared the protocol, but there is at least a chance they could be active as a backup. item.title: Tom Brady Returns To Broadcast Patriots Game Sunday
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The legend walks back into Gillette Stadium, but not as the man who threw the passes, according to Sports Illustrated . Tom Brady will serve as a broadcaster for the first time on Sunday, calling the Patriots game against the Green Bay Packers. This marks a major shift for the seven-time Super Bowl champion, who has skipped calling his old team since joining FOX Sports in 2024. The network finally puts him in the booth for this matchup, ending a long dry spell of him avoiding New England on air. Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd that the moment feels heavy. This week, Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd, “It’ll certainly be emotional,” and he plans to focus on the team’s culture rather than his own past glory. The plan is to show fans how the program works right now. This approach fits a team that has moved past the dynasty years and is building something new under coach Mike Vrabel. Vrabel Keeps It Light Head coach Mike Vrabel took a different view when asked about his former teammate. He played eight years with Brady and won three Super Bowls together. Instead of getting emotional, Vrabel joked that he would handle their catch-up over a video call. He noted that he expects to see Brady in person soon at Rob Gronkowski’s Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. The banter shows a comfortable relationship between the two men. Vrabel knows the history, but he is focused on the present season. The Patriots are 5-3 and looking to build momentum after a win in Miami. Weather and Rivalry History The game faces a different kind of pressure from the sky. Apple Weather projects an 80% chance of rain for the area on Sunday. Most of the water is expected to fall before the game starts. By the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, the forecast calls for only a 20% chance of rain. Fans should bring a jacket as temperatures drop into the upper 40s by the end of the game. This matchup also carries deep history for both sides. The Green Bay Packers have not won at Gillette Stadium since 2002. Both teams have 18 playoff appearances since the NFL realigned in 2002. New England holds the league lead with 40 playoff wins, while Green Bay ranks third with 37. The two franchises have combined for 19 NFL championships. A New Era for the Patriots Brady’s return highlights how much the team has changed. He is no longer the quarterback on the field, and he does not run the offense from the sidelines. His statue stands outside the stadium, but the current roster has its own path. Former tight end Rob Gronkowski will be honored during halftime of the game. The broadcast will be the first time Brady calls a game for his former team. He has been back twice since retiring, once for his Hall of Fame induction and once for the statue unveiling. This Sunday, he brings a new perspective to the broadcast booth. On Sunday, Nov. 8, the Patriots will host the Packers, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m.

item.title: South Works Stadium Dream Is A Money Trap For Bears Fans
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developer Curt Bailey is pushing hard to build the Chicago Bears stadium at the Old U.S. Steel South Works site on the South Side. He sees a skyline view and a boat ride to the venue as the perfect draw. But this flashy pitch ignores the cold hard math that drives NFL decisions. The team needs a deal that saves money, not one that adds billions in costs just to look good on a map. Bailey claims almost $1 billion of work is already happening there, including new university buildings and a hospital. “You can’t help but think this is where the Bears should be,” Bailey said, according to Yahoo Sports . That $1 billion figure sounds impressive until you look at who pays for it. The Bears are currently focused on Indiana because the state offered real tax breaks. Chicago politicians are now scrambling to write new laws to stop the team from leaving. Governor JB Pritzker says his office met with team leaders this week to get legislation ready for a vote in the veto session. “This is part of a continuing endeavor to try to make sure we have legislation ready to go for the veto session hearings on it the first week and a vote the second week of veto,” Pritzker said. The rush to keep the team in Illinois is a political move, not a business one. The Money Chaser Stadium expert Marc Ganis sees the real reason developers are circling the South Works site. They want profit, not football. For years, Ganis has observed that the Bears collaborated with the Arlington Heights government and have already cleared 300 acres of land there. “The fact that developers are starting to circle this tells me that they think there’s a chance it could happen because all they really want is to make money,” Ganis said. A private developer wants to cash in on the project, which means the Bears would lose control and likely pay more. The team already has the land in Arlington Heights ready to go without an intermediary asking for a cut. The Bears say they are still looking at two sites in Hammond, Indiana, while keeping the door open for Illinois options. The team stated they have a duty to look at every option available. “The Chicago Bears remain committed to building a world-class stadium and mixed-use district for our fans, the Chicagoland community and the team,” the Bears said in a statement on Friday, according to Yahoo Sports . But the core issue remains: Indiana offered a deal that works, and Illinois is trying to catch up with new laws. The South Works plan adds a layer of private financing that the Bears do not need. Stick to the Plan The Bears are coming off a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night to improve their record to 6-2. They face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next on Sunday night. The team has momentum and a young quarterback named Caleb Williams who has thrown just one interception this season.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith Says Alabama Is Done If They Lose To LSU
item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Stephen A. Smith is done pretending Alabama deserves a spot in the big dance. The ESPN analyst went hard on Friday, calling out head coach Kalen DeBoer for failing when the stakes are highest. The team sits at No. 5 in the latest rankings with two losses already on the board. A third defeat on Saturday would likely knock them out of the playoff picture for good. Smith Calls Out DeBoer’s Big Game Failures Smith told viewers on ESPN’s “First Take” that the program always gets a pass until it doesn’t. “We always sit up there and crown Alabama,” Smith said, according to Yahoo Sports . He pointed to a string of bad showings that prove the team crumbles under pressure. They lost badly to Indiana in the playoffs and got crushed by Georgia in the SEC Championship Game. They lost to Georgia at home in a thriller this year. He observed that the squad was beaten by Tennessee with “boat-raced” and has now suffered consecutive regular-season defeats for the first time since 2007. In that loss to Tennessee, Alabama accumulated only 201 total yards and committed four turnovers. Smith doesn’t care that DeBoer matched Nick Saban’s win record through 33 games. “Not a d— bit,” Smith said about what his record meant. “Means nothing to me. Nothing.” LSU Ready to Strike While Alabama Bleeds Star linebacker Whit Weeks is doubtful for Saturday due to a fibula fracture, yet the team still has hope. Tight end Trey’Dez Green is listed as questionable after returning from a knee injury. Alabama is hoping to get back starting wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and center Racin Delgatty, both of whom are probable after injuries against Georgia. item.title: Rob Gronkowski’s GOAT Tight End Case: How Patriots Legend Set Standard at Position
item.description: Rob Gronkowski’s GOAT Tight End Case: How Patriots Legend Set Standard at Position originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Rob Gronkowski's legacy continues to linger on gridirons across the country five years after his swansong. The former Patriots and Buccaneers standout was, at his pinnacle, football's greatest tight end, a devastating blend of speed, size and precision who gashed more than a few secondaries across his 11 seasons in the top-flight. Five years after his retirement, Gronkowski's impact continues to loom. So much so, in fact, that some feels he's not only the greatest tight end they have ever laid eyes on; he might be the greatest to ever play the sport. With that, NESN examines Gronkowski's legacy, incluing whether he can truly be considered football's greatest-ever tight end. Rob Gronkowski’s GOAT Tight End Case There is ample statistical evidence that Gronkowski is the greatest tight end in NFL history. While Gronkowski "only" ranks sixth all-time in receiving yards and 11th all-time in receptions among tight ends, he places third in yards per game among tight ends to start at least 50 games, trailing only Travis Kelce and Pete Retzlaff, per Stathead . He recorded 92 touchdowns in his career, the third-highest mark in league history. However, the two players in front of him — Antonio Gates (116) and Tony Gonzalez (111) played 62 and 126 more games than Gronkowski did, respectively. His 9.7 yard per target mark ranks second among tight ends, one yard greater than that of Kelce. He also boasts more the joint second-most first-team All-Pro selections for a tight end (four), tying Kelce, Dave Casper and Shannon Sharpe in the mark. He accomplished that feat in fewer games than his counterpart. With nearly a handful of Super Bowl rings — three with the Patriots, one with the Buccaneers — Gronkowski also proved his worth when the lights were brightest. He ranks second all-time in catches (98), receiving yards (1,389) and receiving touchdowns (15) in the postseason, trailing only Kelce. To be sure, Gronkowski isn't the only candidate for the title of football's greatest-ever tight end. Kelce has an equally compelling case. Perhaps the Chiefs standout makes up for his slight disadvantage in Super Bowls (for now) by posting gaudy numbers over a longer period of his career. Other notable talents who can reasonably challenge for the throne include Gonzalez, Gates and Sharpe. Nevertheless, Gronkowski is arguably in pole position for the crown. That will suit him — and New England supporters — just fine. item.title: Eagles Cut Dameon Pierce As Injury Woes Mount
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles have officially parted ways with running back Dameon Pierce. The team reached an injury settlement with him on Friday night, according to NBC Sports Philadelphia’s Dave Zangaro . The injury settlement reached with Pierce on Friday night clears him off the injured reserve list and makes him a free agent immediately. It is the latest blow for an offensive line that has struggled to find any rhythm this season. Pierce was signed early in the offseason to be the primary backup for Saquon Barkley. He played in three games before suffering an undisclosed injury in Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys. In that loss, he had 14 carries for 47 yards and one touchdown. His departure leaves the roster thin as the team prepares to host the New York Giants on Sunday. A Position in Crisis His departure represents a complete collapse of depth at the running back spot rather than just a single player loss. The Eagles placed Pierce on IR on October 28, making him the third running back to go on the list this season. Reports said that Dameon Pierce was placed on IR by the Eagles., making him the third RB to land on IR this season. The list of injured backs includes Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, both currently on IR. Saquon Barkley is also dealing with back and hamstring issues. The team promoted Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to replace Pierce, but the depth chart is now dangerously shallow. Elijah Mitchell remains available as a practice squad option, but the main rotation is severely compromised. Statistical Reality Check Pierce’s numbers in Philadelphia were modest but showed promise. His short stint concluded with 37 carries yielding two touchdowns and 96 rushing yards. Furthermore, he recorded seven receptions for 14 yards while seeing 11 targets. Before the Eagles, he rushed for 939 yards as a rookie with the Houston Texans. At 25, he appears to have sufficient tread remaining for another squad to gamble on him. The timing of this release is critical. The Eagles are currently in the midst of a six-game losing streak. Creating running lanes has been a major struggle for the unit. Without a healthy backfield, the team cannot sustain drives or generate explosive plays. Next Steps in Philadelphia The focus now shifts entirely to Sunday’s matchup against the Giants. The game is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field. Joe Milton III has been named the starting quarterback, and he needs every bit of help he can get. Barkley has managed to play through his injuries, but his snap count has been limited in recent weeks. Blue remains on the active roster to provide immediate depth. The team is also waiting for the potential return of Bigsby and Shipley later in the season. Pierce’s release allows both sides to move forward without the long-term commitment of injured reserve. Before their Week 10 bye, the Eagles are scheduled to face the Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will both start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix [Reuters] Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also have grid penalties, 10 places for Leclerc and five for Russell. Hamilton initially had only a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season, but the new internal combustion engine that was fitted on Saturday morning failed in final practice. That meant Ferrari decided to fit an entire new power-unit to his car, hence the bigger penalty. Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc and Russell have both fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalty for Leclerc is bigger than Russell's because it is the first time Ferrari have exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Qualifying is set to be wet, after rain started about an hour before the session, and it is expected to continue overnight, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." item.title: Como director addresses the future of former Real Madrid duo amid return links: ‘When the time comes, we will manage the situation’
item.description: Como director addresses the future of former Real Madrid duo amid return links: ‘When the time comes, we will manage the situation’ The two players Real Madrid have sent to Como have both flourished astonishingly well, and while they were always top prospects, Cesc Fabregas has done a phenomenal job in shaping their profiles. Nico Paz and Jacobo Ramon, both have become critical pillars in Como’s project and stellar run in the UEFA Champions League so far. They have not only been playing one of the most attractive brands of football in Europe’s top five leagues but have also surpassed all expectations, and it is clear that Paz and Ramon are both on Real Madrid’s radar. After all, both players provide solutions to departments Los Blancos are currently lacking in, and are world-class options in their own right. Como official speaks Como’s sporting director Carlalberto Ludi spoke to the media in a recent interaction where he was asked about the possibility to Real Madrid taking back both players from the club in the upcoming transfer windows. Nico Paz is in red-hot form. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) He first began by admitting that Real Madrid could well return to the scene, as has been recorded by the media constantly in all recent transfer windows. “I have to put myself in the position of Como supporters, because every November and March, discussions about the possible sale of players begin due to interest from other clubs,” he said, as quoted by Defensa Central . “Whether because of media speculation or other reasons, it always seems as though Real Madrid are ready to bring back all their former players,” he added. Elaborating on how Real Madrid are looking to bring back both players and how media have accurately captured the pulse, he said, “This year, people have started talking about Jacobo Ramón, but over the next two seasons, it will undoubtedly be Nico Paz’s turn.” Ramon is on Real Madrid’s radar again. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Ludi also openly spoke on the business Como and Real Madrid did last season for Nico Paz and how it was a great move for the club. “The truth is that we did good business last summer because Nico Paz is now 100% a Como player.” “That said, Real Madrid have a buy-back option that remains valid until a certain date during the transfer window, as is customary,” he added. Finally, he spoke on how Como would swallow the pill if Real Madrid come back to sign Paz next summer, which is their last chance to keep hold of the player. “If they exercise that option, it would be a sale that would validate the work we have done and would be important for the club. When the time comes, we will manage the situation just as we have done over the past few years.” “We have an excellent relationship with Real Madrid, but for now, we need to enjoy having this footballer with us. He is a champion,” he concluded.
